subject.title: [Bug] Gateway swallows user-visible reply when an agent's exec stdout matches "configuration file" — replies=2 puts ⚠️ 🛠️ first, the actual reply second

question: For successful turns that contain assistant-visible text plus a retained exec-like `lastToolError`, should OpenClaw suppress the channel warning by default, append it after the answer, or keep the current safety-first warning behavior?
rationale: Current code intentionally surfaces mutating-tool warnings even after assistant text, while the reported UX argues that false or recovered exec warnings should not pre-empt the actual reply; automation cannot choose that product/safety tradeoff safely.

options.title: Suppress recovered exec warnings by default
options.body: Treat exec-like `lastToolError` as non-user-visible after a successful assistant reply unless timeout, middleware, verbose, or no-reply conditions require warning output.

options.title: Append warnings after answers only
options.body: Keep mutating-tool warning visibility but require channel ordering and card merging that never puts the warning above a committed assistant answer.

options.title: Keep current safety-first policy
options.body: Leave broad warning visibility in place and rely on narrower classifier fixes, live repro evidence, or explicit config to handle false positives.

recommendation.title: Suppress recovered exec warnings by default
recommendation.body: Treat exec-like `lastToolError` as non-user-visible after a successful assistant reply unless timeout, middleware, verbose, or no-reply conditions require warning output.
